full_details: You stood through Septuagesima at St Helen's. Master Thwaite turned the sand-glass twice and came to his fourteenthly on Lent. Sir John Spencer sat three rows ahead and did not speak to you. At the lodging the penny loaf was a finger short of the notch, the week's sixpence for firing and washing was entered, and your board was threepence. Gib lay on the book. After three you wrote to Anne and set her question first. You will come at Lent, before Mid-Lent Sunday, and you did not name the day. You told her the comedy in four lines and said the ladies have the better of it. The sheet waits for the carrier of the 27th. You struck a London story out of last Sunday's draft. On the comedy's last page you marked a pause and left the ladies' refusal where it was.
one_sentence: You went to St Helen's, heard Lent named, ate at the lodging, and wrote Anne that you will come before Mid-Lent Sunday.
title: Heard Lent named and wrote Anne of Mid-Lent
